ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: Chan teachers pair the killing blade with the life-giving sword to name contrasting capacities of a phrase, shout, blow, or other encounter; later comments assess named teachers as possessing one, both, or neither.
EvidenceBody: Yuanwu Keqin calls the pair an ancient model and a present pivot, then states the contrast in reversed terms: killing does not injure a hair, while giving life costs body and life. Wansong Xingxiu says Linji regularly used the killing blade and also possessed the life-giving sword.

Tianyin Yuanxiu and Jie'an Wujin close spoken turns with the pair. Dabei Miaoyun accompanies it by striking his staff, while Juelang Daosheng criticizes a predecessor as possessing only the killing blade and thereby missing an abbot's larger task. These uses make the expression an evaluative action-image, not a literal weapon report.

Senses.Note: Seven exact witnesses in seven independent works support the paired action-image; the entry does not assign one fixed action pattern to every occurrence.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: The blade is deployed as one side of a paired capacity enacted and evaluated in encounters.
DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: The corpus varies the vehicle and verdict, and even reverses ordinary expectations; no single literal act or fixed action pattern can be imposed on every witness.

DifferentThingTest.Reason: Each uses the same killing-blade image within the killing/life-giving contrast.

DraftEvidence.AliasRationale: Aliases cover the blade image, its regular paired expression, and likely English lookup forms.

ModifierControls.Finding: 殺人 modifies 刀 as a blade's killing function; it does not identify a literal victim in these witnesses.

FamilyControls.Finding: Regular paired counterpart; retained as a related term rather than merged into the headword.
